audits.title: Development and Implementation of a Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis Protocol in the Rehabilitation Setting – A Completed Audit Cycle
audits.standard: NICE: VTE risk assessment within 24 hours of admission; HSE VTE Prevention Programme template
audits.setting: Three rehabilitation wards, St Mary's Hospital, Phoenix Park, Dublin

cycle1.result: VTE risk assessment on admission 0%; therapeutic anticoagulation continued 23 (56%); appropriate prophylaxis started 3 (7%); 8 eligible at-risk patients had no prophylaxis.

audits.intervention: VTE Prophylaxis Protocol based on the HSE template incorporated into the admission booklet on 3 pilot wards (February 2024).

cycle2.result: VTE risk assessment within 24 hours 10 (40%); anticoagulation continued 9 (36%); appropriate prophylaxis 5 (20%); 3 at-risk patients had no prophylaxis; 1 inappropriately received prophylaxis.

audits.other_findings: No association between prophylaxis prescribing and protocol use was shown in this small sample.
audits.citation: Synnott P, Hamaty J, Perrira N, Frindunbekov Y, Khalid M, McCarthy F. Development and Implementation of a Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis Protocol in the Rehabilitation Setting – A Completed Audit Cycle. Age and Ageing. 2024;53(Supplement_4). doi:10.1093/ageing/afae178.180.

audits.title: 894 An Audit of Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis in A Busy ENT Department
audits.setting: Adult ENT ward, emergency and pre-operative admissions (NHS GGC, Glasgow)

cycle1.result: VTE risk assessment clearly done for 39%; 22/63 (35%) meeting LMWH criteria received it; 5/96 (5%) meeting TEDS criteria received it; 45% had both prescribed according to the guideline

audits.intervention: Planned only: departmental policy and staff education
audits.other_findings: Pro-forma clerking (n = 148) improved risk assessment compared with freehand clerking (n = 25) (43% vs 12%) but not correct prescription (45% vs 40%); no VTE or unexpected bleeding occurred.
audits.citation: Connelly A, Williamson A. 894 An Audit of Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis in A Busy ENT Department. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.111.

audits.title: 1368 TED Talks and Fragmin Shots: Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis (VTEP) in a busy Emergency Surgical Unit (ESU) - A Quality Improvement Project
audits.standard: National guidelines: all surgical admissions risk assessed for VTE within 24 hours
audits.setting: Emergency Surgical Unit, Northwick Park Hospital

cycle1.result: VTE risk assessment complete 54%; LMWH prescribed 57%, TEDs prescribed 37%; 26% wearing TEDs.

audits.intervention: Three PDSA cycles: educational poster; VTE e-learning module and inter-professional tutorials; patient information leaflet distributed with TEDs.

cycle2.result: Patient adherence to TEDs 64%, with sustained improvement in all other parameters.

audits.other_findings: After cycle 1 (October 2020, n=68) VTERA 73.5%, LMWH 75%, TEDs 53%; after cycle 2 (November 2020, n=55) all parameters improved except TED wearing (31%).
audits.citation: Sharma A, Siddique H, Oyeyipo Y, Sajorda L, Nadeem U, Watfah J, et al.. 1368 TED Talks and Fragmin Shots: Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis (VTEP) in a busy Emergency Surgical Unit (ESU) - A Quality Improvement Project. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.777.

audits.title: EP.FRI.258 A closed loop audit of deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis in the acute surgical receiving unit of a large teaching hospital; reducing morbidity and mortality, and improving cost-effectiveness
audits.standard: Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network VTE prophylaxis proforma (LMWH and anti-embolic stockings)
audits.setting: Acute surgical receiving unit, Queen Elizabeth University Hospital, Glasgow (large teaching hospital)

cycle1.result: 13.9% did not receive LMWH when indicated; 37.4% non-compliant with AES; overall 40% had insufficient thromboprophylaxis (171 patients across both cycles).

audits.intervention: Reinforcing importance of VTE prophylaxis to junior doctors and nurses, and posters in the department and on patient trolleys.

cycle2.result: 8.9% did not receive LMWH when indicated; 46.4% non-compliant with AES; overall 50% had insufficient thromboprophylaxis.

audits.other_findings: LMWH compliance rose by 5.0% but AES compliance fell by 9.0% on re-audit.
audits.citation: Chen J, Norman F, Paterson-Byrne P, Nicholson G. EP.FRI.258 A closed loop audit of deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis in the acute surgical receiving unit of a large teaching hospital; reducing morbidity and mortality, and improving cost-effectiveness. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab312.048.

audits.title: EP.FRI.495 A retrospective audit of electronic venous thromboembolism risk assessment compliance across three surgical wards in a district general hospital
audits.standard: VTE risk assessment within 24 hours of admission and reassessment within 48 hours (aim 100%)
audits.setting: Three surgical wards, Hereford County Hospital, district general hospital

cycle1.result: First assessments within 24 hours above 65%; second assessments within 48 hours 36.1%; breast 95.3%, colorectal 90%, general surgery 86.6%.

audits.intervention: Results presented at departmental meetings and educational posters displayed.

cycle2.result: Second assessments within 48 hours 47.6%; breast 100%, colorectal 93.3%, general surgery 88.0%; first assessments within 24 hours remained above 65%.

audits.other_findings: Variation between wards persisted; next step is making the late-shift FY1 responsible for outstanding assessments.
audits.citation: Banwaith T, Qayum M, Arun C, Nawaz G. EP.FRI.495 A retrospective audit of electronic venous thromboembolism risk assessment compliance across three surgical wards in a district general hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab312.082.

audits.title: EP.FRI.835 5 Years, 4 F1s, 3 Registrars, 2 Pandemic Waves, 1 VTE audit: Half a decade of VTE prophylaxis on a surgical ward
audits.standard: VTE risk assessment and prophylaxis at admission

cycle1.result: VTE risk documented in 92%; enoxaparin prescribed for 96%; TED stockings 96%.

audits.intervention: Induction VTE teaching, HCA VTE champions, digital reminders and monthly email reminders after successive cycles

cycle2.result: VTE risk documented in 53%; enoxaparin 73%; TED stockings 73%.

audits.other_findings: Five annual cycles: risk documentation 92%, 65%, 57%, 76% and 53% (2017-2021), with a drop during the first pandemic wave; electronic prescribing with mandatory VTE checklists has begun.
audits.citation: Sylvester H, Slim N, Okocha M. EP.FRI.835 5 Years, 4 F1s, 3 Registrars, 2 Pandemic Waves, 1 VTE audit: Half a decade of VTE prophylaxis on a surgical ward. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab312.124.

audits.title: 81 An Audit of Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) Risk Assessment & Prophylaxis Implementation
audits.standard: NHS Standard Contract: 95% of inpatients VTE risk assessed; NICE NG89

cycle1.result: VTE risk assessment completed in 72.1%, accurate in 15.4%; prescription rate 84.6%, prescribing accuracy 41.2%.

audits.intervention: Mandatory VTE prescribing training for all junior doctors joining the trust

cycle2.result: Risk assessment completion 94.2%, accuracy 34.5%; prescription rate 90.6%, prescribing accuracy 79.5%.

audits.other_findings: Paediatric, obstetric and ITU patients were excluded.

audits.title: 416 Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis in Emergency Surgical Admission: The Power of a Checkbox in Reducing Errors. a Closed Audit
audits.setting: General surgery emergency admissions, University Hospital Galway

cycle1.result: Of 36 eligible, 29 adequately treated with chemoprophylaxis and 7 under- or overtreated for weight and renal clearance; 35 of 40 charted for TED stockings.

audits.intervention: Educational presentation and two checkboxes added with pharmacy to the prophylactic anticoagulant page of the drug chart, prompting weight and renal function.

cycle2.result: 37 of 38 eligible received weight and renal function-adjusted doses; all 40 received TED stockings.

audits.title: 1263 Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) Risk Assessment and Thromboprophylaxis Among Hospitalised Patients: A Single-Centre Closed Loop Audit
audits.standard: NICE NG89: all patients risk-assessed for VTE on admission and re-assessed at consultant review; NHS Standard Contract
audits.setting: Large teaching hospital, University Hospitals Bristol and Weston Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: VTE risk assessment completion 16.67%; median time to re-assessment 97 hours.

audits.intervention: Use of technology for VTE risk assessments, mandatory teaching sessions and prompts in clerking proformas.

cycle2.result: VTE risk assessment completion 100%; median time to re-assessment 21 hours.

audits.other_findings: Positive feedback on the interventions was received.

audits.title: 752 VTE Prophylaxis and VTE Assessment Form in Plastic Surgery: A Closed-Loop Audit
audits.standard: Trust VTE risk assessment guideline and form; target 100% compliance
audits.setting: Plastic surgery inpatients staying longer than 24 h, Sheffield Teaching Hospital

cycle1.result: Chemoprophylaxis prescribing 69.5%; VTE risk assessment form used 0%; inappropriate chemoprophylaxis 18.8%.

audits.intervention: Results presented at departmental meeting; VTE checkbox added to handover list; posters in doctors' office with VTE forms attached.

cycle2.result: Chemoprophylaxis prescribing 95%; VTE form used 70%; inappropriate chemoprophylaxis 8%; mechanical prophylaxis increased by 15.8%.

audits.other_findings: 100% target not met; electronic VTE assessment recommended because of junior doctor turnover.

audits.standard: Local trust guideline on weight- and renal function-adjusted VTE prophylaxis
audits.setting: Emergency general surgery department, Ashford and St Peter's Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: 49 (86.0%) prescribed per guideline; of 8 non-adherent, 5 (62.5%) had no prophylaxis and 3 (37.5%) incorrect doses.

cycle2.result: 39 (90.7%) adhered; no dosing errors, but 4 (9.3%) had no prophylaxis prescribed.

audits.other_findings: No bleeding or thromboembolic complications in either cycle; omissions did not improve.

audits.title: 946 Post-Operative Venous Thromboprophylaxis: An Audit on Departmental Compliance with Association of Breast Surgery (ABS UK) Recommendations
audits.standard: Association of Breast Surgery (ABS UK) recommendations on chemoprophylaxis in high-risk groups; national VTE risk <0.4%
audits.setting: Breast surgery under one consultant (Ysbyty Gwynedd, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board, Bangor)

cycle1.result: No VTE in any patient (compliant with national risk <0.4%); only two patients received chemoprophylaxis despite 11 with anaesthetic >3 hours and 22 with predisposing conditions

audits.other_findings: 119 (73.5%) operations were for malignancy; one patient was imaged for suspected pulmonary embolism and was negative.

audits.title: 270 An Audit Looking at the Peri-Operative Management of Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis in Surgical Patients Under the Upper Gastrointestinal Team at Royal Liverpool University Hospital
audits.standard: VTE prevention guidelines (risk assessment, prescription accuracy and timing)
audits.setting: Royal Liverpool University Hospital, Upper GI surgical team

cycle1.result: 99% risk assessed; enoxaparin prescribed in 84%; 11% received prophylaxis when not indicated and 6% missed it when indicated; appropriate dosing 82%; timing met guidance in 79%.

audits.other_findings: Prophylaxis suspended peri-operatively in 40% (typically two missed doses); stockings prescribed in 87% (93% appropriate); in-hospital VTE 6%.

audits.title: Audit cycle - VTE risk assessment in inpatient wards in mid Essex
audits.standard: Trust policy: VTE risk assessment for every admitted patient (100%)
audits.setting: Inpatient wards in mid Essex (electronic system Paris); cross-sectional study

cycle1.result: 82% completion; 45% completed on day of admission or next day; 34% no documentation of prior prophylactic anticoagulants; 3% no documented outcome.

audits.intervention: Recommendations made to improve completion rate; audit tool updated to reflect changes to the electronic form.

cycle2.result: 95% completion; 74% completed on day of admission or next day; 26% no documentation of prior prophylactic anticoagulants; 7% no documented outcome.

audits.other_findings: The 100% target was still not met.
audits.citation: Abdelkhalek H, Elagawany A, McDowall F, Leahy M, Baker E, Penberton N. Audit cycle - VTE risk assessment in inpatient wards in mid Essex. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S305-S305. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.807.
